title: Handle partial helm apply during operator upgrades via ephemeral config rollback
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers on Private/VPC deployments observed upgrade failures where Helm applied some CRDs and operator resources but failed mid-way (timeout or API server transient error). The result is a partial operator rollout: new controller images are registered but webhook/certs or CRD versions are inconsistent, leaving tenant controllers in a degraded state (reconcile loops, webhook 429/403). This ticket proposes an automated ephemeral-config rollback mechanism plus a targeted hotfix to the helm preflight/apply logic to detect and safely nudge failed partial applies into a coherent state without requiring full tenant rollbacks or operator uninstall.

Context and impact: 3 escalations in the last 7 days (support cases #13812, #13845, #13903). Symptoms include webhook failures, operator reconcile storms, and failed post-upgrade nodeagent enrollments. Short-term mitigations (manual kube-applier steps) are labor-intensive and risky; customers expect a non-destructive automated remediation and a hotfix patch to reduce recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy onprem operator v2.6.4 to a fresh tenant namespace with existing CRD v1alpha1
2) Start helm upgrade with --wait and artificially throttle API server (kubectl proxy with rate limit) until the upgrade times out after CRDs applied but before webhook configs are reconciled
3) Observe operator pods with new image, webhook failures (403/429), and CRDs in mixed versions (spec.version mismatch),
4) Check tenant controllers enter crashloop/reconcile storms and some webhook requests return 'admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1' mismatch errors
acceptance_criteria: 1) New operator upgrade flow can detect 'partial apply' state via a deterministic probe (CRD version skew + webhook.ConfigMap mismatch) within 90s of failure

2) Ephemeral-config rollback will revert only the in-flight operator resource manifests (mutatingwebhookconfiguration, validatingwebhookconfiguration, operator Deployment) to the previous stable revision without touching tenant workloads or persistent data
3) Automated remediation succeeds in >= 95% of internally simulated partial-upgrade scenarios in our CI upgrade harness
4) Provide a minimal runbook and one-click console action for Solutions to trigger the rollback for a customer
5) Hotfix release operator-2.7.1 applied to hosted smoke clusters and two pilot customers with zero regressions observed in 48h
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Patel: Ticket created after SOC + Support triage. Captured three escalations and initial logs. Assigned to Diego for investigation.

2026-02-19 Diego Ramirez: Reproduced locally by throttling API server. Confirmed partial CRD apply + webhook mismatch. Created small POC script that calculates CRD version skew and webhook checksum differences.

2026-02-20 Ava Chen (SRE): Ran POC against upgrade harness with 50 simulated tenants; observed automated rollback success in 42/50 runs. Failures correlated with ephemeral admissionregistration write errors—need retry backoff.

2026-02-21 Diego Ramirez: Design decision to implement ephemeral-config rollback as a two-step reconcile: detect->snapshot previous operator manifests->apply rollback if stable probe fails. Preparing PR with migration-safe annotations.
2026-02-23 Liam O'Connor (Support): Drafted customer communication template and one-click console button text. Coordinating pilot with customer acme-corp and beta-tenant-7.
2026-02-24 Maya Patel: Security review waived for rollback codepath (no secret material). Moving to implementation and QA. Added to release operator-2.7.1-hotfix.
2026-02-24 Diego Ramirez: Linked PR opened and integration tests added. Still tuning exponential backoff on webhook re-create to avoid rate limiting the API server.
decisions: 1) Implement detection heuristics first (CRD semantic version mismatch + webhook configuration checksum delta) instead of relying on helm release state alone
2) Snapshot only operator control-plane manifests (Deployments, WebhookConfigurations, ServiceAccounts) for rollback; do not touch tenant CRs or Secrets
3) Provide opt-in console action for Solutions and an automatic remediation mode for Dedicated accounts with SLA escalation disabled
4) Limit automatic rollback attempts to 3 retries with exponential backoff to avoid compounding API server pressure
notes: Hotfix release will include improved helm preflight checks: API server liveness probe before CRD apply and additional jitter on helm hooks
We will schedule a customer pilot window (UTC 03:00-07:00) to minimize impact and coordinate with oncall SRE
